topicName: Probabilistic Data Structures (HyperLogLog, Bloom Filters, Cuckoo Filters)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Probabilistic Data Structures in Redis: HyperLogLog, Bloom Filters, and Cuckoo Filters"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When scaling modern web applications, memory efficiency is paramount. Exact counting and membership testing over massive datasets consume vast amounts of RAM. Redis provides native and modular probabilistic data structures that trade absolute precision for exponential memory savings. This tutorial covers the mechanics, commands, and practical use cases of HyperLogLog, Bloom Filters, and Cuckoo Filters within Redis."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. HyperLogLog: Cardinality Estimation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"HyperLogLog (HLL) is an algorithm used to estimate the cardinality (number of distinct elements) of a set. A traditional set tracking 1 billion unique user IDs would require gigabytes of RAM. Redis HLL achieves this using a fixed memory allocation of just 12 KB per key, with a standard error of less than 1 percent."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"PFADD unique_visitors:2023-10-25 "user_101" "user_102" "user_103"
PFADD unique_visitors:2023-10-25 "user_101" "user_104"
PFCOUNT unique_visitors:2023-10-25"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also merge multiple HLL structures to calculate the union of distinct sets without re-processing the raw underlying data."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"PFMERGE unique_visitors:october unique_visitors:2023-10-24 unique_visitors:2023-10-25
PFCOUNT unique_visitors:october"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Bloom Filters: Scalable Membership Testing"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Bloom Filter tells you whether an element is *definitely not* in a set, or *probably* in the set. False positives are possible, but false negatives are impossible. Powered by RedisBloom (a Redis module), Bloom Filters are ideal for avoiding expensive database lookups for non-existent keys (e.g., checking if a username is already taken)."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"BF.RESERVE user_emails 0.01 10000
BF.ADD user_emails "alice@example.com"
BF.EXISTS user_emails "alice@example.com"
BF.EXISTS user_emails "bob@example.com""},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The first argument after the key in BF.RESERVE is the desired error rate (0.01 for 1 percent)."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The second argument is the expected capacity of items."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Cuckoo Filters: Deletion and Space Efficiency"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Bloom Filters are space-efficient, standard Bloom Filters do not support item deletion without rebuilding the entire filter. Cuckoo Filters solve this limitation by supporting both insertions and deletions while frequently outperforming Bloom Filters in memory usage for low-to-moderate false positive rates."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"CF.RESERVE active_sessions 100000
CF.ADD active_sessions "session_xyz123"
CF.EXISTS active_sessions "session_xyz123"
CF.DEL active_sessions "session_xyz123""},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Trade-offs"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"HyperLogLog: Best for counting unique items with minimal memory. Does not support element retrieval or deletion."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Bloom Filters: Best for fast set membership checks. Supports addition, but no deletions."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cuckoo Filters: Best for dynamic datasets requiring both membership testing and item deletion."}]
